title: clinvar_classification() returns another allele's record for a multi-allelic rsID
description:
`clinvar_classification()` keeps the first UID that esearch returns (`pkg-r/R/clinvar.R:240`). For an rsID that covers several alleles, that can be another allele's record. The help page says so, but its own example shows it: `clinvar_classification("rs113488022")` returns the record for BRAF V600G, not V600E.

```r
d <- biohttp::body_or_null(bioclients::clinvar_classification("rs113488022"))
d[, c("uid", "accession", "title", "significance")]
#>     uid    accession                                     title significance
#> 1 40389 VCV000040389 NM_004333.6(BRAF):c.1799T>G (p.Val600Gly)   Pathogenic
```

esearch returns `40389, 13961` for this rsID. VCV000013961 is V600E, whose germline classification is "Conflicting classifications of pathogenicity".

This is the bug variant-reviewer shows on its BRAF V600E example today (samuelbharti/variant-reviewer#27), so it would come along with #35.

## Proposal

Give callers a way to name the allele, for example an optional `hgvsp` (or `allele`) argument. With it, the function fetches the summaries for all UIDs and keeps the one whose title has that protein change. Without it, it returns every matching record, or keeps today's behaviour with a warning when there is more than one.

The example in the help page could use V600E's own term once that exists.

title: mygene_gene() and mygene_genes() return NA ensembl_gene for PTEN and MUC16
description:
`mygene_gene()` and `mygene_genes()` return `NA` for `ensembl_gene` when MyGene maps a gene to more than one Ensembl id. PTEN and MUC16 are two examples: MyGene sends their `ensembl` field as a list of objects, where the second id is on an assembly patch.

```
PTEN   [{"gene": "ENSG00000171862"}, {"gene": "ENSG00000284792"}]   second id on HG2334_PATCH
MUC16  [{"gene": "ENSG00000181143"}, {"gene": "ENSG00000291738"}]   second id on HG2461_PATCH
NF1    {"gene": "ENSG00000196712"}
```

`pkg-r/R/mygene.R:153` reads it with `biohttp::pluck_at(hit, "ensembl", "gene")`, which returns `NULL` on a list of objects, so `mygene_first()` gets nothing.

## Reproduce

With bioclients 0.1.1 from CRAN:

```r
d <- biohttp::body_or_null(bioclients::mygene_genes(c("PTEN", "MUC16", "NF1")))
d[, c("symbol", "entrez", "ensembl_gene")]
#>   symbol entrez    ensembl_gene
#> 1   PTEN   5728            <NA>
#> 2  MUC16  94025            <NA>
#> 3    NF1   4763 ENSG00000196712
```

`mygene_gene("PTEN")` gives the same `NA`.

## Fix

When `ensembl` is a list, read `gene` from each element and keep the id on the primary assembly (`ENSG00000171862` for PTEN, `ENSG00000181143` for MUC16). A test with this response shape would keep it fixed.

genescout and variant-reviewer carry the same read: samuelbharti/genescout#48.

title: 0.1.1 has no Zenodo archive
description:
CRAN and r-universe both serve 0.1.1. Zenodo holds one record, for 0.1.0.

```
concept DOI   10.5281/zenodo.21770870
v0.1.0        10.5281/zenodo.21770871
v0.1.1        none
```

`CITATION.cff` matches what Zenodo has, so it is correct rather than stale. The
gap is the archive itself.

Zenodo mints a DOI from a GitHub release, so a version tagged without one gets no
record. Anyone citing the version they actually installed has nothing to point
at, and the concept DOI resolves to 0.1.0 rather than to the newest release.

The README used to name 0.1.0 as the version to pin, which was true and read as
though it were current. That sentence is gone in #36. The archive is still a
release behind.

title: Move variant-reviewer onto biohttp, then onto bioclients
description:
`variant-reviewer` still carries its own HTTP layer and its own client for each service. Removing
that duplication is what bioclients was built for. The work splits in two halves.

## Move the HTTP layer onto biohttp

A working demo exists. Swapping the transport touched one file, left the eleven API clients alone,
and passed the app's whole suite at 340 of 340, with live calls confirmed against four services. It
also turned up three real bugs in `biohttp`, fixed in 0.1.1.

The change has not landed.

## Move the clients onto bioclients

Not started, and the bigger half. `variant-reviewer` has one client per service today, and those
clients are the copies bioclients exists to replace.

## Why this is here

Both halves were listed in the README as roadmap rows. A README states what a package is now, so
the plan moved here where it can be updated without touching the front page.
